title: sdks: unify auth/retries and streaming ergonomics + parity bump v1.100.0
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Multiple SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) diverged in auth handling, retry behavior, and streaming ergonomics which causes inconsistent developer experience and intermittent production bugs. This PR unifies auth middleware, standardizes retry semantics (idempotency, backoff, and header propagation), improves streaming API ergonomics (backpressure, cancellation, and reconnect), and bumps SDK versions to v1.100.0 across languages.

Summary of changes: - Python: introduce UnifiedAuth + RetryMiddleware, fix streaming generator cancellation, and add simpler async/iter API. - TypeScript: harmonize auth hooks, fix streaming backpressure handling for fetch/Node streams, and export higher-level streaming helpers. - Go: add auth-retry wrapper, and improve client Stream(ctx) cancellation semantics. - Repo-level: update changelogs, CI matrix to include new test permutations, and version bumps for release.

Checklist: - [x] Implement unified auth middleware in all SDKs - [x] Standardize retry policy and expose config on client constructors - [x] Address streaming cancellation/backpressure across runtimes - [x] Add cross-language integration tests and unit tests - [x] Update CHANGELOGs and release notes - [x] Bump package versions to v1.100.0

Compatibility notes: The default retry policy is backward compatible with previous behavior for non-idempotent endpoints; we add opt-in stricter idempotency checks. Streaming API surface is additive: new ergonomic helpers are exported while existing low-level stream objects remain available. Customers using custom auth middleware should switch to the new UnifiedAuth shim (compat adapter provided).

Testing: added 34 new unit tests, 6 integration tests across runtimes. Local converged test matrix run in CI (Linux/macOS, Node 18/20, Go 1.20/1.21, Python 3.10/3.11) with flaky streaming test fixed by adding explicit heartbeat and reconnect logic.

Release notes: see release_notes field.

Related: ENG-2345 (SDK parity initiative), ARCH-998 (streaming reliability improvements).
commits: fix(python): cancel streaming generator on client.close() to avoid leaked tasks
feat(ts): export streaming helpers + harmonize auth hook interface
fix(ts): apply backpressure to fetch ReadableStream, handle Node environmental differences
feat(go): add auth-retry wrapper and Stream(ctx) cancellation improvements
chore(release): bump python/typescript/go SDK versions to v1.100.0
test(ci): add cross-language integration matrix and flaky test fixes
review_thread: Riley Chen: Can you clarify the default retry policy for non-idempotent requests? We need to avoid accidental duplicates (asked 2025-11-14).
Ava Martinez: Default policy mirrors previous behavior (no retries for non-idempotent by default). We added explicit opt-in via client.retry_policy.allow_non_idempotent = true. (reply 2025-11-14)

Samir Patel: TS streaming helpers look great, but in Node the pipeline teardown still left a dangling socket in my local repro. Added a tiny patch to ensure stream.destroy() is called on error. (requested changes 2025-11-18)
Ava Martinez: Applied the Node teardown fix in commit 4. Verified with local Node e2e. (reply 2025-11-19)
Jordan Lee: Please add changelog entries for all 3 SDKs and confirm package signing metadata for Go. (requested changes 2025-11-20)
Ava Martinez: Changelogs added and Go signing metadata included. (reply 2025-11-21)
Riley Chen: CI showed intermittent failure on streaming heartbeat test — I reran and it passed. CI looked green after the fix. Approved. (approved 2025-11-28)
release_notes:
- SDKs: unified auth middleware across Python/TS/Go
- SDKs: standardized retry semantics and opt-in non-idempotent retries
- SDKs: improved streaming ergonomics (cancellation, backpressure, reconnect)
- Bugfixes: streaming generator cancellation leaks, Node socket teardown
- Version bump: v1.100.0 for Python/TypeScript/Go
notes: This is a broad parity and ergonomics PR intended to reduce operational surprises for multi-language customers. Post-merge: follow up task to publish packages to registries and coordinate staged rollouts for Dedicated/Private customers.
